ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Banco de Espana PEP register (transposition of Directive (EU) 2015/849), the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, and the Spanish terrorism-linked individuals register (Real Decreto 1867/1998). Enhanced due diligence and senior management approval are required for any PEP match, FATF high-risk third-country residence, or negative media hit. Continuous adverse-media and sanctions re-screening must occur at least every 12 months per SEPBLAC guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Certificacion Negativa de Denominacion Social via, the Sede Electronica del Registro Mercantil Central (Colegio de Registradores de Espana) - www.registradores.org / www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be in Spanish or any co-official Spanish language using Latin script (Castilian, Catalan, Basque, Galician). Foreign-language names are admissible only if transliterated into Latin characters and directly express the corporate activity or a lawful trade object. Symbols, signs, leading abbreviations, and expressions contrary to law or public policy are prohibited per Article 404 RRM.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Holding (requires evidence of genuine holding activity)
Internacional (requires documentary evidence of cross-border operations)
Espana or any Autonomous Community or municipal name without prior administrative authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central Technical Office rejects the proposed name, the applicant (through a lawyer or procurador) may file a written administrative appeal (recurso) within one month of notification before the Direccion General de Seguridad Juridica y Fe Publica of the Ministerio de Justicia, or alternatively re-submit a distinct name via the RMC portal. If the rejection arises from a prohibited or sensitive token, prior ministerial authorization must be obtained from the competent ministry. If the appeal is denied, judicial review may be sought before the Audiencia Nacional within two months. To mitigate delay, applicants should simultaneously submit two to three backup name proposals at the statutory fee per name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for registration purposes only where the registered address is an accredited corporate domiciliation service in a provincial capital; a mere PO Box or non-physical virtual mailbox is not acceptable. For aviation asset dry-leasing (ISIC 5223), the Spanish corporate substance expectation is moderate, requiring the SL to maintain effective administration, accounting records, and decision-making presence in Spain; a pure letterbox leasing vehicle will face elevated CFC, ATAD, and substance-challenge risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium: approximately 25-35% annual probability of a documentary substance review by SEPBLAC/MINECO and an unannounced on-site inspection by the Agencia Tributaria during the first two years of operation, given the high-value mobile asset profile and cross-border wire-rail payments; the probability falls to approximately 10% after evidence of real local management and economic activity is established.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Companies Act), Articles 1–22 (incorporation formalities, public deed and registry registration), Articles 23–31 (mandatory statutory content and registered office rules), and Article 62 (minimum paid-up capital of €3,000 for the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (corporate name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office jurisdiction (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid for deed filing and company registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) containing the articles of association, executed before a Spanish notary and filed with the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SL requires minimum nominal capital of €3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation; cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked Spanish bank escrow account (certificado de depósito) or with the notary, and the escrow certificate must be attached to the public deed; in-kind contributions require a statutory expert valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Board Resolution adopted at the inaugural meeting of the sole shareholder of [COMPANY], Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, in Madrid, on [DATE]: FIRST — The share capital of €3,000, represented by 100 equal participation interests, is deemed fully subscribed and paid in as evidenced by the annexed bank escrow certificate. SECOND — The registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], Madrid, under the jurisdiction of the Registro Mercantil de Madrid. THIRD — [NAME], NIE [NIE], is appointed Sole Administrator with full powers to manage assets, open escrow bank accounts, negotiate and execute aircraft engine leasing agreements, and appoint attorneys-in-law. FOURTH — The Administrator is authorized to pursue municipal activity licensing, environmental and occupational clearances, and all tax registrations before AEAT and TGSS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central – online name certification portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official name search application (solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación) electronically, proposing up to three alternative corporate names; the Registry verifies no identical or confusingly similar name is registered and issues the negative name certificate, which is reserved for three months.
required_dossiers: Authenticated or apostilled passport copy of each incorporator
NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) card or proof of NIE application
Power of attorney if a representative files the application
Completed official name certificate application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, resubmit the application using the two alternative names on the same filing; the certification period restarts and remains valid for three months from issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Deposit of Minimum Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (bank) or the chosen notary's cash escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-resident business account in the name of the company under formation or in the name of the subscriber, deposit the full subscribed capital (minimum €3,000) as a blocked escrow holding, and obtain the bank capital deposit certificate addressed to the notary; alternatively, deposit the funds with the notary under his escrow protocol.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate issued by Registro Mercantil Central
NIE or passport of each subscriber
Banking KYC and beneficial ownership declaration forms
Proposed company identification and address data for the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines account opening on residence grounds, use the notary's escrow mechanism or request the certificate from a bank designated by the notary; the blocked status must remain evidenced until registry registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary (Notaría) in the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the name certificate, bank escrow certificate, subscriber identity documents and the draft bylaws (estatutos) to the notary; the notary reviews legal capacity, reads and authenticates the deed, which records corporate form (SL), object (aircraft engine dry-leasing), registered office, share capital, participation interests and appointment of the Sole Administrator; the notary issues the authorized first copy for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bank escrow capital deposit certificate
NIE or passport copies of all incorporators
Draft articles of association and allocation schedule of participation interests
Proof of registered office availability (premises title or lease offer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to statutory contents or capital evidence, correct the bylaws or obtain a rectified bank certificate and re-execute the deed; any re-execution follows the notarial fee scale and does not void prior valid declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provisional NIF and Tax Census Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Delegación de Hacienda of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 (declaración censal) together with an authorized notarial copy of the deed; AEAT assigns the provisional NIF (prefix ES followed by the assigned code plus letter); simultaneously complete the capital formation tax payment (Modalidad de Operaciones Societarias under the Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados, at approximately 1% of nominal capital) at the competent regional treasury using the applicable Model 600/620/621 forms.
required_dossiers: Authorized notarial copy of the deed of incorporation
Form 036 declaration
Identity documents of the sole shareholder and appointed administrator
Lease agreement or proof of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT queries the censal filing, re-file the complete Form 036 attaching the rectified deed copy; provisional NIF issuance is same-day upon compliant re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office jurisdiction (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authorized notarial copy of the deed with the Registro Mercantil, together with proof of settlement of the corporate formation tax; the Registrar examines the deed's legality, publicizes the corporate existence and issues the registration certificate (inscripción) which completes the SL's legal personality; publication also follows in the BORME.
required_dossiers: Authorized notarial copy of the deed of incorporation
Proof of payment of the capital formation tax (ITP-AJD / Operaciones Societarias)
Negative name certificate
Power of attorney or authorization for the filing representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a qualified objection (calificación), correct the deed through a new notarial act or supplement the missing documents; a gubernative appeal lies to the General Directorate of Registries and Notaries if the objection is unlawful.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain its definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from AEAT before starting operations, using Form 036 or 036/030 and presenting the deed of incorporation at the local tax office. Non-resident foreign entities without a permanent establishment must appoint a tax representative and apply for a non-resident NIF using Form 030; for EU residents, Form 036 is used. The VAT number for Spanish businesses is the NIF preceded by 'ES' for EU cross-border transactions. Foreign trading companies acquiring or leasing Spanish assets should also verify whether a permanent establishment is triggered under Article 13 of the Ley del Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - Spanish-resident SL is subject to corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on worldwide income; it is not a pass-through entity. Profits distributed to shareholders are separately taxed as dividends unless participation exemption applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not offer US-style check-the-box elections or unilateral hybrid-mismatch elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) application of the Spanish tax group consolidation regime under Article 61 of Ley 27/2014 (LIS) by qualifying Spanish entities holding at least 75% (or 70% if listed) of accessible share capital; (ii) the special intra-group neutrality regime for qualifying transactions; (iii) installment methods for corporate income tax payments; and (iv) optional regimes such as the ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) and patented box for qualifying IP. Hybrid mismatches are controlled by Articles 61-62 LIVA and Article 15 LIS in line with ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), governed by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA) and Royal Decree 1624/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for established Spanish taxable persons; registration is compulsory before the first taxable supply or acquisition. For intra-EU distance sales to final consumers, the Spanish threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year for the Optional VAT Mini One Stop Shop / One Stop Shop. Non-established EU and non-EU suppliers providing electronically supplied services or other B2C digital services to Spanish consumers use the OSS regime regardless of threshold; non-established taxpayers supplying goods or services in Spain must register as from the first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Immediate Information Supply (Suministro Inmediato de Información - SII) is mandatory for taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000, for those under the medium-size regime, and for taxpayers in the VAT group or filing periodic declarations for goods supplied to the Canary Islands. SII requires real-time electronic transmission of invoicing records to AEAT via web services (API, SOAP/REST) within four calendar days of issuance (with deadline extension to eight days if excessive). Spain is phasing in mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under the Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece): all invoicing software must be certified and invoice records must be made available to AEAT via Verifactu; full B2B e-invoice obligation and interoperable platform will be fully compulsory for all businesses by the relevant transition calendar. Digital fiscal stamping and cryptographic hash chains are required for billing software; paper invoices remain allowed for certain exempt/simple activities but must comply with VeriFactu.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to third countries and territories are subject to 0% VAT ('exemption with right to deduction') under Article 21 LIVA. The exporter must physically remove the goods from Spain and the EU/ES customs territory within the statutory period (generally 3 months from dispatch), hold valid customs export declaration, transport documents, and commercial evidence. Intra-EU supplies of goods to a taxable person with a VAT number are zero-rated under Article 25 LIVA if transport to another Member State and the customer's valid VAT ID are evidenced. Aircraft engine dry leasing to a foreign airline or lessee qualifies as VAT zero-rating only if the engine is physically exported from the EU, or is an offshore service subject to the place-of-supply B2B rules under Article 69.3 LIVA (customer established outside Spain/EU outside EU) that exempts the service if directly related to aircraft or aircraft engines intended for international traffic or if the recipient is outside the EU. For dry leasing of aircraft engines used for international air transport, the supply can be exempt under Article 24 LIVA (international traffic) if the aircraft/engine is used for international routes and adequate evidence is kept.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Unified Administrative Document (DUA) / Customs Export Declaration
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds in Spain
Commercial invoice and leasing contract containing parties, asset identifiers, terms, and agreed export destination
Proof of physical departure from EU customs territory (bill of lading, port/airport handling receipt, delivery note)
Certified evidence of customer identity when claiming zero-rating as an intra-EU supply (customer VAT registration certificate)
Aircraft engine maintenance log and export-related NIL state of movement where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT tax audits target fraudulent export VAT zero-rating and phantom exports. Incorrect application of zero-rating or failure to retain required proof of export results in reversal of the VAT deduction, assessment of 21% VAT on the supply, late-payment interest, and penalties under Article 191 LIVA and Articles 183-193 LGT. Substantial infringements are penalized at 50%-150% of the tax omitted (100% where fraudulent means or false invoices are used, or 150% for recidivist behaviour). Suspended declaration without real export or sham leasing contracts may incur penalties up to EUR 300,000 in addition to criminal exposure under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code if the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000. The claim period is four years from the return due date; clawbacks may be imposed retrospectively if the supporting customs/transport evidence is falsified, raised after payment or not adjusted in supplementary returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is Spain’s central bank and national authority for specified external-payment and balance-of-payments reporting. Spain’s foreign-exchange framework also derives from EU law and Spanish legislation administered by the competent Spanish authorities, including the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business. Banco de España does not generally pre-approve routine foreign-exchange transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is an EU and euro-area member. The euro is freely convertible, and capital movements and current international payments are generally unrestricted, subject to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, prudential rules, and reporting obligations. There is no general approval requirement for an SL to receive foreign investment, pay foreign suppliers, or remit dividends or other lawful profits. Dividend distributions remain subject to Spanish corporate-law requirements, including distributable-reserve, net-equity, corporate-approval, and applicable withholding-tax rules. Banks may request evidence of the transaction’s purpose, source of funds, beneficial ownership, tax compliance, and supporting contracts. Cross-border transaction or position reporting to Banco de España may apply under the external-transaction reporting regime; applicable thresholds, periodicity, and filing responsibility should be confirmed against current rules and the company’s transaction profile.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds within a prescribed period or convert a mandatory percentage into euros. Export receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to applicable reporting, sanctions, tax, accounting, and bank AML/KYC requirements. The SL should retain export invoices, transport and customs evidence where applicable, customer contracts, and bank records to substantiate receipts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplementary payment services, subject to the provider’s Spanish or EU authorization, service scope, and the SL’s risk profile. An authorized EU electronic money institution may provide payment or e-money services under its applicable authorization and passporting rights, but e-money is not a bank deposit and is not covered by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund as a bank deposit. An EMI account may not satisfy a bank’s, counterparty’s, or transaction’s requirements for a conventional corporate bank account, escrow, trade finance, or commercial letter of credit. Confirm safeguarding arrangements, permitted currencies, SWIFT access, local IBAN availability, limits, and aircraft-industry acceptance before reliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors appear physically at a bank branch to open a corporate account. Banks determine onboarding methods under risk-based AML/KYC controls; remote onboarding may be available but is not assured, particularly for nonresident or complex ownership structures. Expect the bank to require company formation and registration records, Spanish tax identification numbers, proof of registered office and business activity, beneficial-owner information, director and signatory identification, source-of-funds evidence, and potentially an in-person or video interview. Foreign documents may require apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation. A bank may require a Spanish-resident representative, additional due diligence, or branch attendance as a condition of acceptance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nonresident, layered, or trust ownership; difficulty identifying the ultimate beneficial owner or persons exercising control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registers and constitutional documents for each ownership layer; certified ownership chart to natural persons; beneficial-owner declarations; identity and address evidence; control agreements and trust instruments where applicable; apostilles or legalization and sworn translations where required; explanation of any nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unexplained shareholder funding, third-party capital contributions, or transfers from jurisdictions inconsistent with the stated ownership or business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription and shareholder-loan agreements; board or shareholder resolutions; originating bank statements and payment confirmations; audited financial statements, tax returns, sale or financing documents supporting source of wealth and funds; transfer-purpose narrative; evidence linking remitter, investor, and SL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aircraft-engine leasing payments, unusual counterparties, payments routed through unrelated jurisdictions, or mismatch between lease terms and cash flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed lease and maintenance agreements; engine and counterparty identification; invoices and payment schedules; aircraft or engine ownership and delivery records; lessee and beneficial-owner KYC; sanctions screening results; evidence of commercial purpose, operational location, insurance, and relevant tax treatment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned, high-risk, or conflict-affected jurisdictions, or parties with adverse media or opaque ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented sanctions and adverse-media screening; complete counterparty and beneficial-owner records; transaction route and end-use evidence; export-control assessment where relevant; legal review and any required authorization. Do not process a prohibited transaction or attempt to evade sanctions controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated company with no trading history, material forecast turnover, or a business model inconsistent with the stated activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and cash-flow forecast; incorporation and tax registrations; office or operating-address evidence; lease pipeline and customer letters; management biographies; expected countries, currencies, volumes, and counterparties; explanation of initial funding and projected payment flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity and shareholder-loan funding from an account in the investor’s own name to the SL’s Spanish corporate account, using SWIFT or SEPA as applicable and accurately identifying the remitter and beneficiary. Spain does not generally require a foreign-exchange license or a universal capital purpose code for an ordinary capital transfer. Provide the bank with the subscription or loan agreement, corporate approvals, incorporation records, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, and a clear payment reference such as share capital contribution or shareholder loan. Coordinate any required capital registration, accounting, tax, and Banco de España external-transaction reporting with Spanish advisers. Do not use third-party remitters or split transfers to avoid controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the scheme limits and bank availability; use SWIFT cross-border credit transfers for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. SWIFT MT103 is the traditional customer-credit-transfer message; banks are transitioning to ISO 20022 messaging, so confirm the bank’s current format and required payment data. Include accurate beneficiary, bank, invoice, contract, currency, and payment-purpose information and retain confirmations. For engine acquisitions or other qualifying trade transactions, a commercial documentary letter of credit may be arranged through a bank, subject to credit approval, underlying transaction documents, and applicable UCP rules. Escrow is contractual and bank/provider-dependent, not a general Spanish FX-control requirement. Screen counterparties and banks for sanctions and obtain customs, tax, and supporting trade documentation where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards, generally for documented or otherwise bank-accepted exposures and subject to counterparty credit, suitability, and documentation requirements
Non-deliverable forwards where offered and legally available for the relevant currency and counterparty; settlement and regulatory treatment depend on the instrument and counterparties
Foreign-exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps, subject to bank approval, applicable collateral and documentation terms, and EU derivatives requirements
Options and other permitted FX derivatives where offered by an authorized counterparty and appropriate for the company’s classification and documented risk-management policy

Derivatives involving EU financial counterparties may be subject to EMIR reporting and other applicable risk-mitigation, clearing, or margin obligations; the company should confirm its classification, thresholds, reporting responsibility, and any delegated reporting arrangement before execution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 4 months after financial year-end (typically 30 April for calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 300,000 EUR and potential company dissolution
Penalties of 100-10,000 EUR plus surcharges and possible criminal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each quarterly period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 10,000 EUR per return plus interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of any change in ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 100,000 EUR for non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if net turnover exceeds 2 million EUR, total assets exceed 1 million EUR, or average employees exceed 50

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual review and update of UBO information required; changes must be notified within 1 month to the Registro Central de Beneficiarios Finales

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 50-250 USD annually for registered office in Spain
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500-6,000 USD for standard SL; 5,000-15,000 USD for complex aviation leasing operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created SLs (sociedades de nueva creacion) subject to 15% CIT on their first two tax periods with a positive taxable base; small-sized taxpayers (net turnover below EUR 10 million) taxed at 23% on the first EUR 5 million of taxable income and 25% on the excess; R&D and technological innovation credits up to 42% of qualifying expenditure; patent box regime providing a 60% exemption on qualifying IP income; capitalisation reserve deduction (reserva de capitalizacion) of 10% of the increase in equity, capped at 10% of taxable base; Canary Islands ZEC regime offering a reduced 4% CIT rate for eligible aircraft leasing undertakings with genuine substance and annual commitment thresholds (not applicable to the mainland SL).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite) since the 2015 tax reform; the former 15-year and 18-year limits were abolished. Annual offset is quantitatively capped at 70% of taxable income for taxpayers with net turnover of EUR 20 million or more, 60% for taxpayers with turnover between EUR 1 million and EUR 20 million, and an absolute unrestricted floor of EUR 1 million per tax year is always available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 - Impuesto sobre Sociedades (annual Corporate Income Tax return); filed exclusively by electronic means through the AEAT Sede Electronica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) using an electronic certificate. Quarterly advance payments are made on Modelo 202; withholding tax declarations on non-resident distributions are made on Modelo 216 (or Modelo 123 for domestic payees) and refund claims on Modelo 210.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing on Modelo 200; three mandatory quarterly advance payments (pagos fraccionados) on Modelo 202 due 1-20 April, 1-20 October and 1-20 December each year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 must be filed within 25 calendar days following the end of the six-month period after the corporate tax year closes; for a calendar-year SL the return is due by 25 July of the following year. If the day falls on a non-working day, the deadline shifts to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Identification module (NIF, corporate name, domicilio fiscal)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification for the Spanish-resident SL: NIF assigned by AEAT, registered name, main address and economic activity code (CNAE/ISIC 5223 mapping to aircraft and spacecraft leasing).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files under its own NIF; no foreign branch statement applies unless the SL has a permanent establishment abroad, in which case Box 2 requires the PE identification and the declaration of attributed income. The foreign parent is not a signatory on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 107-108 (Base imponible: resultado contable ajustado y compensacion de bases imponibles negativas)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit with taxable income: add-back of non-deductible expenses (financial goodwill, entertainment, penalties), adjustments for the participation exemption on exempt lease dividends, depreciation of aircraft engines per Art. 12.1 LIS, and offset of prior-year tax losses in accordance with Art. 26 LIS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a resident SL the reconciliation is made entirely from Spanish GAAP books. Non-resident shareholders never enter these boxes; any claim relating to the SL's taxable base must be raised by the SL itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 109-110 (Tipo de gravamen y cuota integra)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the applicable CIT rate: 25% general rate; 15% for newly incorporated entities in their first two profitable years where the activity is genuinely carried on with employees and premises; 23% for small-sized taxpayers on the first EUR 5 million of the taxable base; 30% for entities with turnover exceeding EUR 20 million in force for periods commencing on or after 1 January 2025 (global minimum top-up context).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no interest in these boxes. However, if the SL remits its taxable profits abroad as dividends, the 19% withholding tax (or treaty-reduced rate) arises as a separate obligation reported by the SL on Modelo 216.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 615 / Declarative table of related-party transactions (pagina de operaciones vinculadas)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of cross-border and domestic transactions with related parties: dry-leasing fees paid or received for aircraft engines, currency swap payments, escrow balances, management charges and interest; the chosen transfer pricing method must be stated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For engine leases between the Spanish SL and a foreign affiliate, report the counterparty NIF/identification, the country of residence, the amount, and the arm's length method used (typically CUP or TNMM because turbofan engine rental comparables exist at engine-repair shop and leasing-platform level). A non-resident parent with a permanent establishment interacting with the SL must also file its own TP form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 124-130 (Deducciones por doble imposicion, bonificaciones y deducciones para incentivar determinadas actividades)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim of the domestic and international double-taxation relief: credit for taxes paid by foreign subsidiaries or PEs, the R&D credit, the job creation credit, and the patent-box deduction on IP embedded in lease contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SL receives lease income from foreign lessees, any foreign income tax withheld abroad may be credited in Box 124; non-resident shareholders cannot claim credits on the Spanish return and must instead invoke the DTA refund mechanism via Modelo 210.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 134-160 (Deuda tributaria: cuota resultante y liquidacion)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the final tax payable or refundable after applying withholdings, instalments, and payments made in the preceding quarterly Modelo 202 statements; the net amount is paid by SEPA direct debit referenced in Box 160.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL's own return is not the vehicle for taxing the foreign parent. Upon asserting a dividend distribution, the SL must operate WHT on the gross distribution pursuant to Article 25.1 LIRNR, file Modelo 216 within the following 25 days, and remit the tax to the AEAT. The non-resident parent separately claims treaty relief by refund on Modelo 210 or by advance recognition of the treaty certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior request: surcharge of 5% of the tax due if filed within 3 months of the deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (3.75% for the relevant periods); formal sanction under Article 198 LGT of EUR 200-EUR 6,000 for erroneous or incomplete declarations; underestimation penalties under Article 191 LGT of 50%-150% of the omitted amount; if the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax year, criminal liability under Article 305 of the Criminal Code with imprisonment of 2-6 years and a fine of double to six times the defrauded amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% of the gross dividend paid to non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment in Spain (Article 25.1.a) LIRNR); increased to 24% where the recipient is resident of a territory classified as non-cooperative for tax information exchange. Dividends paid to EU/EEA parent companies satisfying the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (5% shareholding held for at least 12 months) are exempt from Spanish withholding where the parent files the corresponding certificate; Spanish domestic participation exemption (Article 21 LIS) equally requires a 5% holding and a 12-month holding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate (illustratively, 5% under the U.S.-Spain DTA for a corporate parent owning at least 10% of the voting rights): (1) before the dividend payment date, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the Spanish SL (or its designated escrow or paying agent) an original or certified Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by its home tax authority (for U.S. parents, IRS Form 6166 with attached schedule) covering the year of the distribution; (2) the certificate must evidence residence, beneficial ownership, and, where the DTA requires, the absence of entitlement abuse; (3) the SL, acting as payer, applies the reduced rate at source and reports the payment and the rate applied on Modelo 216 within 25 days after the quarter-end; (4) where the statutory 19% was withheld because the certificate was unavailable at payment, the non-resident must file Modelo 210 requesting a refund of the excess, attaching the TRC and a statement of effective taxation; the claim is time-barred after four years from the end of the statutory filing period; (5) Spanish-language translation or apostille is required when the certificate is not in Spanish and is not covered by the EU administrative cooperation regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest paid by the Spanish SL to non-residents without a permanent establishment is 19% (Article 25.1.b) LIRNR), rising to 24% for payments to recipients in jurisdictions without an effective exchange of information. Treaty relief: under the U.S.-Spain DTA as amended by the 2013 Protocol, payments for the right to use industrial, commercial or scientific equipment (the classification of an aircraft engine dry-lease fee) are treated as royalties and capped at 5% (where the old 4% rate was subsumed for qualifying equipment rentals); interest is capped at 10% generally, 5% for interest beneficially owned by a bank or insurance company with respect to loans concluded for a term exceeding seven years; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive limits withholding to 10% for associated enterprises holding 25% of the capital, provided the beneficial owner is an EU company with genuine establishment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Master File, Local File and the Spanish TP study) is required where: (i) the SL's net turnover in the tax period equals or exceeds EUR 10 million; or (ii) the aggregate amount of related-party transactions concluded in the tax period exceeds EUR 1,000,000; or (iii) a specific transaction or homogeneous series of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000. Where the turnover threshold is met, documentation is obligatory even for small balances. Simplified documentation applies to transactions with related parties when the entity's turnover is below EUR 10 million and the transaction type thresholds are not exceeded; in all cases the arm's length standard of Article 18 LIS and OECD TPG 2022 govern the price-setting for aircraft engine dry-leasing fees, lease deposits, residual-value guarantees and linked financing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing akin to the UAE, but enforces an equivalent economic substance doctrine through Article 15 LGT (conflict in the application of tax law), the EU ATAD general anti-abuse rule (Article 15 bis LGT), and the 'valid economic reasons' test in Articles 18.2, 21 and 100 LIS. For an aircraft engine dry-leasing SL, substance is demonstrated by real administrative and commercial personnel in Spain, genuine decision-making by the directors, physical office facilities, actual lease negotiation and risk-management functions, sufficient capitalisation, and the absence of circular financing. A letter-box SL that merely invoices lease revenue or parks tax-exempt dividends for a foreign parent without staff or premises will be recharacterised: the dividend, royalty or leasing income may be reattributed to the shareholder, treaty and directive benefits denied, and the adjustment penalised. The SL must also maintain a robust transfer pricing file evidencing that its residual-value risk, maintenance liability and insolvency exposure genuinely correspond to its contractual role as lessor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion (Article 305 Criminal Code)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing Modelo 200 with fabricated profit figures, inflating depreciation deductions on turbofan engines, concealing lease premiums received through escrow, falsely offsetting ineligible tax losses or using artificial structures to move profits to a related party in a low-tax jurisdiction; the criminal threshold is defrauding the Spanish public treasury of more than EUR 120,000 per tax year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 2 to 6 years, a fine of double to six times the defrauded amount, loss of the right to obtain subsidies or public aid, and publication of the sentence; in the administrative route, a penalty of 50%-150% of the omitted tax plus late-payment interest of 3.75% annually, with the additional prohibition on contracting with public administrations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise or participate in the fraudulent filing are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt (Article 42.2.c) LGT) and may be separately prosecuted; criminal conviction leads to personal fines, disqualification from managing companies of up to 10 years, provisional detention and passport withdrawal while the proceedings are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificiality and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Spanish SL with no employees, no business premises, or no genuine aviation asset management activity, while directing all material decisions from the foreign parent; channelling engine lease income through the SL solely to claim the Spanish participation exemption or a beneficial DTA dividend rate; entering into back-to-back leases without assuming real operational risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under Articles 15 and 15 bis LGT of the transaction as performed by the beneficial owner, denial of the participation exemption, disallowance of treaty benefits, reassessment of the taxable base, penalty of up to 150% of the assessed amount, and in egregious cross-border cases the NIF may be revoked and the entity struck from the commercial register as a sham.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly establish or maintain the artificial structure are jointly liable for the additional assessment and sanctions; the corporate veil is pierced so that directors' personal assets, bank accounts and residences may be seized; if the artificiality is used to evade the EUR 120,000 threshold, directors face criminal prosecution for aggravated evasion with imprisonment of 2-6 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting lease payments or engine sale proceeds through Swift Wire or Escrow Accounts without conducting adequate customer due diligence; failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the lessee; failing to report suspicious transactions connected to sanctions evasion, aircraft fraud or third-party money laundering; using escrow arrangements to conceal the origin of funds in excess of EUR 10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines scaled as minor (up to EUR 60,000), serious (EUR 60,001-EUR 150,000) and very serious (EUR 150,001-EUR 5,000,000); criminal laundering under Article 301 of the Criminal Code is punishable by 6 months to 6 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to three times the laundered value; aggravated sanctions apply where the offence is committed in a professional capacity or through a corporate vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors and the designated compliance officer are personally liable for AML failures; wilful blindness to the origin of lease payments can ground a criminal conviction for complicity in money laundering, disqualification from acting as director, travel bans related to the criminal proceedings, and joint civil liability for the confiscation of laundered assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Arm's Length Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or submit the Master File and Local File despite exceeding the EUR 1,000,000 aggregate or EUR 250,000 transaction-type thresholds; setting dry-lease rates for aircraft engines to foreign affiliates at materially below market CUP or TNMM reference levels; failing to provide documentation during an AEAT audit of the residual-value risk and profit allocation; charging artificial management or financing fees to strip taxable basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment (ajuste primario) of the difference between the agreed price and the arm's length price, plus a penalty of 15% of the amount of the adjustment if the taxpayer did not correctly document the valuation; independent penalty for failure to provide documentation of 1% of net turnover, minimum EUR 300 and maximum EUR 2,000, and where the related-party transaction is with a tax-haven entity a penalty of up to 2% of the transaction value. Interest accumulates at 3.75% on the assessed shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who instructed or failed to supervise the preparation of the TP file are jointly and severally liable for the adjustment, penalties and interest; deliberate cross-border manipulation of the lease margin may be treated as an offence of defrauding the treasury, making directors personally criminally liable and subject to disqualification from managing Spanish companies.
